thread.title: Apple (AAPL) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Apple (AAPL) 3rd Quarter Earnings: What to Expect
text:
iStock photo
Can a strong Apple ( AAPL ) earnings report stop the decline in tech stocks? That is one of several questions Wall Street expects to get an answer to Tuesday.
The iPhone maker is the only remaining FAANG name — Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) — that has yet to report earnings. And it will do so Tuesday when it releases third quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing bell. Already the world’s most valuable company, Apple has an outside shot to be the first to reach a valuation of $1 trillion — a mystical benchmark by every measure.
And the likelihood that Apple can achieve this feat before FAANG peers Amazon and Google is just icing on the cake.
In the three months that ended June, Wall Street expect the Cupertino, Calif.-based tech giant to earn $2.18 per share on revenue of $52.34 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to $1.67 per share on revenue of $45.41 billion. For the full year, ending October, earnings are expected to rise 25% year over year to $11.48 per share, while full-year revenue of $261.16 billion would rise 13.9% year over year.
Apple last quarter issued revenue guidance to come in the range of $51.5 billion to $53.5 billion. While the mid-point of that range would translate to a 15% decline from the Q2’s $61 million revenue total, that’s also because consumers typically wait for new iPhone releases that are due to come out in the fall. "This quarter takes a back seat to the 'main event' which is all about the FY19 underlying iPhone demand picture and ramping services business which remains a key incremental growth driver for Cook & Co. for the coming years," Daniel Ives, analyst at GBH Insights.
In other words, there won’t be any surprises this quarter. But there will be questions in the other areas of the report, namely how many iPhones — particularly the more expensive iPhone X — did Apple sell? In the fiscal Q2 the average selling price of iPhones rose 11% YoY to $728, driving Apple Q2 revenue to $61.1 billion, up 16% year over year, while profits soared 25%. Launched last fall at a price of $999, the device was a part of Apple’s super-cycle, drawing expectations of massive phone upgrades reminiscent of the iPhone 6’s success in 2015.
As it stands, iPhone revenue now accounts for 62% of total sales. Wall Street expects that Apple sold 42 million iPhones in the third quarter, while generating some $30 billion in iPhone revenue. But will this be the quarter that Services revenue, which has a current run rate of $33.4 billion and includes Apple Music, the App Store and Apple Pay, take a bigger step forward? Services has grown to become Apple's second-largest business, while delivering the highest profit margins.
Beyond these topics, investors will listen for clues about product releases for the holiday quarter and overall guidance about fiscal 2019 to gauge how confident Apple feels about its product lineup. Discussions about capital allocation and increasing its stock buyback — all of which can accelerate the pace of achieving the $1 trillion market cap.
